Images were captured using two smartphones, a Redmi Note 10 and a Samsung M31, under the fluorescent lighting of the college canteen between 12:30 and 14:00 on weekdays, and under mixed daylight at home on weekends. Plates were photographed from directly above at a height of approximately 40 cm. Dishes that were partially hidden by other items were still annotated, provided that at least half of the dish was visible. Annotation was carried out in LabelImg using the YOLO text format. Of the 712 images collected, 12 were discarded because of motion blur, leaving 700 images containing 3,184 labelled dish instances across 12 classes. The most frequent class was rice, with 611 instances, and the least frequent was rasam, with 74. To limit class imbalance, rasam and kadhi images were oversampled by a factor of two during training. The model was trained for 50 epochs on a laptop with an Intel i5 processor and 16 GB of RAM, which took 6 hours and 20 minutes. Inference on a single image took 410 ms on the same machine.
